relevance_note: The paper reports three cohort patients with mosaic (not germline) TNFAIP3 variants: "Three patients with lymphoproliferation had mosaic variants in TNFAIP3 leading to premature termination and haploinsufficiency (Patient IDs 66, 99, and 507)".
method_note: Read the whole paper (text, Tables 1-4, figure legends; the remainder is references) and built the JSON with a short Python script in my scratch directory; every value was taken from my reading and every span was checked by script to occur verbatim. SCOPE: this is a cohort study of 452 affected and 154 healthy individuals screened for mosaic variants in 71/101 immune genes; only the three individuals with TNFAIP3 variants (Patient IDs 66, 99, 507) were extracted. About 60 other individuals in Tables 1-4 carry mosaic variants only in other genes or are healthy controls and were not extracted. All three TNFAIP3 variants are MOSAIC (low VAF), not germline; the paper does not diagnose HA20 in any of them and states that mosaic TNFAIP3 variants have not been demonstrated to cause mosaic GEI. LABELS: the Patient ID column values of Tables 1 and 3 ('66', '99', '507'); the text calls them 'Patient 66', 'Pt. ID 66', 'Patient 99' and 'Patient ID 507'. Tables have patients as rows. AGE: Table 1 'Age' column has no unit or time point; read as years (consistent with text, e.g. Patient ID 89 '48 y.o.' = Table 1 age 48; Patient ID 185 '26 y.o.' = age 26) and recorded as age at last evaluation/time of report, though it may be age at sampling. VARIANTS: no transcript or cDNA is printed; genomic positions are hg38 per the Table 1 column header. Text gives truncated forms 'p. Asn98Lysfs' and 'p.Leu147Glnfs' for the table forms 'p.Asn98LysfsTer27' and 'p.Leu147GlnfsTer7' (not treated as contradictions). VAFs (initial/reseq/ddPCR): 66 0.059/0.057/0.058; 99 0.016/0.0148/0.0162; 507 TNFAIP3 0.060/ND/ND; 507 MAP3K1 0.049/ND/ND. Patient 507 also carries a mosaic MAP3K1 p.Val128Met (UMS), unambiguously attributed in Tables 1 and 3, so recorded. Variant type for 507 comes from its position under the 'Frameshift' (TNFAIP3) and 'Missense' (MAP3K1) section rows of Table 1. Pathogenicity uses the authors' own mosaic scoring (LMP/UMS), not ACMG. 'Functional' evidence is cell-subset enrichment by ddPCR (66, 99); 507 was not tested. PHENOTYPES: Table 3 'Clin. Pheno' categories are LYM (66), DYS (99) and DEF (507), whereas the text says all three had lymphoproliferation (66 and 99 as their main clinical symptom; 507 'a lymphoproliferative phenotype'); this is a difference of category, not a stated absence, so both are recorded and no contradiction rows were needed. 'Immune dysregulation' for 66 and 507 is inferred from 'Symptoms of immune dysregulation were present in all affected individuals'. A lymph node biopsy is mentioned for patient 66 but lymphadenopathy is not stated, so it was not recorded. No other clinical details (onset, treatment, ethnicity, family) are given; Supplemental Table S5 (clinical details) is not in this text. DEDUPLICATION: patient 66's p.Tyr246Ter was also detected by exome reanalysis in 'Ghosh et al. (accompanying manuscript)', so the same patient may appear in that paper; it is described as accompanying, not earlier, so cites_prior_report_of_same_patients was left null.
